canonical_claim: Cross-task coordination for the stabilization plan: within Phase 3, sub-item D1d (removing ShardCoverage::folded_cursor/incarnation) must run before D5 (the gtest_cas_dangling_precommit.cpp rename) since both touch the same `cov.folded_cursor = 7;` test line; Phase-2 task A7 must land before Phase-5 task B3 since B3's gcHealth() reads gc_scheduler under A7's gc_scheduler_mutex.

Deferred refactors explicitly out of scope for the stabilization plan (spec §6): a CasGc.cpp split, de-god-classing Cas::Store, DiskSelector per-disk isolation, DiskObjectStorageTransaction part-path virtualization, removeFileIfExists+writeFile ordering dead code, and a latent MultipleDisks shared_from_this issue.

A BACKLOG item requires a GC per-table recovery gate (abort-only clamp) before the fold extracts manifest edges, because the fold currently trusts codec-valid transactions without state-machine replay; this gate is mandatory before multi-writer or rolling-upgrade-skew milestones ship.; A GC per-table recovery gate (abort-only clamp) was filed as a MANDATORY pre-multi-writer backlog item after round-2 adversarial consults on the wedge-counter fix, alongside a correction of a false "dead surface" annotation introduced by the fix itself.

`build/t5_inventory_before.txt` and `build/t5_inventory_after.txt` (429 lines) were force-committed inside the gitignored `build/` directory; recommended follow-up is `git rm --cached` since the inventory classification already lives in the task report.

Open TODOs in the writer protocol: B172 (S3 staging area + server-side copy to remove the local scratch-dir requirement), the B199-S2 TLA+ gate extending `CaBuildRootPrecommit.tla` for the inline-closure fold barrier, plain non-replicated mutation publish still running under the `data_parts` lock (B151's fix covers only replicated paths), and a `farewell` on graceful shutdown to retire the epoch immediately instead of waiting for K=2 frozen-`seq` GC detection.

`REPLACE PARTITION`/`ATTACH PARTITION ... FROM` queue-clone relink on a Replicated CA table has no dedicated test: `test_cas_replicated_relink` only proves relink for the plain INSERT/merge fetch path, and it is not established which branch a queue-cloned `REPLACE_RANGE` fetch takes; recorded as a scoped BACKLOG test-debt line rather than added to the T12 gate.

A one-shot `CORRUPTED_DATA` error from a temp-fetch with an absent binding was observed once during the definitive consistency soak and flagged for investigation; it was not reproduced or root-caused during the round.

Scenario cards that check GC-reclaim progress mid-run (not just at the final checkpoint) must honor the condemn-grace period the same way the end-checkpoint does, or they miscount in-pipeline objects awaiting graduation as a leak; this miscalibration (not a product bug) caused a false-red S36 verdict and is a lesson for other scenario cards with mid-run reclaim assertions.

As of the 2026-07-03 real-object-storage validation, gate #1 (multi-backend real-store validation) had AWS S3 and GCS both fully validated (probe + replication + two-phase reclaim + fsck clean); Azure had not been started, and GCS's production-grade follow-ups (compose finalize for >1 GiB conditional writes, `gcp_oauth` credential validation, generation-aware LIST discovery) were left as desirable, non-blocking rows.

The §7 dedup-validate-on-hit lever (the forgotten read-class lever, accounting for roughly 73% of HEADs left unreduced) was deliberately deferred to a future round rather than included in the 2026-07-13 optimization round, and recorded in the spec as a §2 follow-up.

A backlogged protocol optimization (PROMOTE-REVALIDATION-MINIMIZATION): the ack-floor model licenses skipping per-leaf promote HEADs when the installed round is unchanged since dependency observation (`DepEntry::observed_view_round`), complementary to the resurrect fixes which cover the recovery path when the round moved mid-commit.

An uncertainty-exhaustion abort class was identified as a backlog item: `putBlob`'s pre-existing 8-round ABORTED loop times the ~90s controller budget can reach roughly 12 minutes worst case, crossing the native `receive_timeout` (300s) around round 3-4 and causing client-side ambiguity; the fix direction is a distinct "uncertainty budget exhausted" abort class that stops the outer ABORTED loop from re-driving a fully exhausted controller envelope.

CA gtest scratch directories leaked at scale — about 50,000 `CasGtestScratch`-family directories exhausted a 1.048M-inode tmpfs and broke an unrelated build; swept the affected suites from ~100% leaking to 14%, with the remaining teardown fix chartered as BACKLOG `[CA-GTEST-TMP-SCRATCH-LEAK]` and deliberately not run while other lane gates are in flight.

D2 deferred S23's 1-server and 10-server idle baselines as INCONCLUSIVE pending multi-topology infra (tied to the S12 10-replica Cluster node-count backlog), and flagged S23's idle RSS at +82 MiB against a 64 MiB budget as likely allocator/log slack requiring confirmation it does not grow unbounded during the 4h soak.

A follow-up triage of the review (deduplicated against Mikhail's comments) sorted the "Verify / Add Tests" bucket into: (1) R1/X1 reader-vs-GC race — for normal MergeTree this is likely covered by DataPart lifetime; action is to document that CAS read safety depends on MergeTree part lifetime and audit whether any ref-less/cross-node reader path actually exists, implementing ephemeral read pins only if such a path is real; (2) replication paths — add CA-specific reconciliation tests for RPL-2 if cheap, add a targeted relink-vs-GC test for RPL-3, recheck the to_detached perf cliff for RPL-4, and treat RPL-5 as coverage debt; (3) W-N3 write-batching liveness — add queue-wait/leader-flush-latency/batch-size/batch-failure metrics first, then make the wait cancellation/timeout-aware only if the numbers show stalls.

The same follow-up triage sorted the "Document / Defer" bucket into: (1) security model — SEC-1 (CityHash128 not cryptographic) is the real concern if a pool crosses trust domains; for release, explicitly document "one CAS pool = one trust domain", and for multi-tenant future add a cryptographic hash mode or trust-domain-scoped dedup, with SEC-2/SEC-3 accepted as by-design under that model; (2) a day-2 runbook (AD-3) should be a table of failure mode to signal/metric to diagnostic command to recovery command to test, covering stalled GC, persistent clamp, lost/corrupt gc/state, live-mount conflict, orphan refs/manifests, pool-meta corruption, and backup/restore of the CAS control plane; (3) low/minor cleanup items R2-R4, W-N4, G-N2 through G-N4, SEC-4/SEC-5 are not urgent correctness blockers but good hardening: cache the manifest under the GET token, assert TTL vs GC latency, configure S3 multipart-cleanup lifecycle, add decode-size caps, and reject `..` in `checkNamespace`.

The archaeology report's 10 open questions requiring owner confirmation before release: (1) whether `root_shards`/`_precommits`/`Store::shardOf` are reserved for future ref-sharding or removable as vestigial after snapshot+log; (2) whether there is a tracking item for the TOKEN⇒CONTENT probe gap; (3) whether any soak dashboards still reference the six dead `ContentAddressed*` ProfileEvents; (4) whether fsck actually classifies and reclaims a leaked pruned-generation prefix from the Task-7 hand-off leak; (5) whether verbatim-file writes via the plain-object CAS helpers are ever on a path where outliving the mount lease matters; (6) whether a dedicated protocol field is planned before release to replace the `part_id` relink cookie; (7) whether `manifest_hash` on the Keeper part znode (listed in ROADMAP as a dedup optimization) is still intended; (8) whether the cache-over-CA `notYet()` stub message (naming a limitation `DiskObjectStorageCache.cpp:29` now handles) still reflects a real gap or is purely stale; (9) whether cross-disk `MOVE PARTITION ... TO DISK/VOLUME` involving a CA disk has been verified, since a code comment admits the path is unverified; (10) whether the standing soak findings (mount-lease race history, S30/S34/S35 gates) have been re-checked against this report's risk register for anything the static analysis missed.

The archaeology report's recommended architectural-correction backlog (§13.3, medium risk/effort, not yet applied): move `IContentAddressedExchange` to a neutral home and fold `parseTableUuid` into `adoptPartFromManifest`; encapsulate the projection whole-part-transaction rule so callers never branch on `isContentAddressed()` directly (kills the B58-class trap, removes 6 duplicated conditionals); route plain-object writes through `CasRequestController` or give them an explicitly-documented exemption; split `CasGc.cpp` (a 2.3k-line unit carrying four redesigns) into workflow units (fold / deletion / cleanup / cursor / budget) keeping `Gc` as pure orchestration; split `Store::open` into explicit create/open-rw/open-ro modes, since a read-only open can still write `_pool_meta` on an empty pool; probe TOKEN⇒CONTENT at startup; and add a dedicated access right for `GC REBUILD` that requires an explicit disk.

The archaeology report's high-risk/uncertain cleanup items needing an owner decision or production evidence before acting (§13.4): removing `root_shards` from `PoolConfig`/`PoolMeta` and `fence_seq` from `GcState` (format changes are cheap pre-release but both may be intentionally reserved, per open question #1); a dedicated wire field for the relink manifest to replace the `part_id` cookie plus a hardened handshake (a protocol change requiring replication-compat coordination); a durable move journal for RENAME TABLE atomicity (real design work, current re-drivable behavior may be acceptable pre-release); a real-concurrency thread-interleaved store/GC test harness (large effort, overlaps TLA+/soak coverage, needs a division-of-labor decision); and an `unlinkFile` committed-content assertion (requires deciding how to represent "whole-part removal in progress" without new state).

The archaeology report's low-risk cleanup backlog (§13.1, stale comments/dead code/dead counters, none yet applied) includes: deleting the dead `_watermark` classification branch and fixing a stale watermark comment (`CasInstrumentedBackend.cpp:129`, `CasStore.cpp:263`); removing the `GcSnapPersist` event husk and the always-0 `CasEvent::round` field (5 write sites) per the project's own no-compat-scaffolding-pre-release rule; fixing the stale key-layout comment in `CasGcOutcomes.h:33-37` referencing the removed `fence_seq` keying and dead line anchors in `CasGcCursorKey.h`; re-pointing/removing comments naming the deleted `Store::shardOf` method (`CasGcShardPlan.h:23`, `CasBuild.h:98,103`); fixing stale column docs in `ContentAddressedLog` for `manifest_expand`/`manifest_strip`/`pack`/`tree` (never emitted); and updating `docs/superpowers/cas/01-architecture.md`'s GC and ref-shard sections to the snapshot+log reality or stamping them historical.

Whether `~Pool()` destruction — deferred when an in-flight transaction holds the last `PoolPtr` — can issue farewell/lease I/O through an already-shut-down object storage is an unconfirmed ordering contract; a best-effort try/catch bounds the blast radius to a swallowed error today, but the ordering guarantee itself was never traced, pending a one-off investigation of `S3ObjectStorage::shutdown` semantics and the table-shutdown drain guarantee.

The claim that default-enabled CAS system logs (`content_addressed_log`, `content_addressed_mounts`) cost zero overhead when no CA disk exists has not been independently traced through the SystemLog flush path; a one-off check (row counts + background flush activity on a vanilla server) is needed before upstreaming the default config.

Mount/lease epoch fencing under real concurrency is exercised only via scripted single-threaded backends plus TLA+ models, not real threads; the P3.1 S13 fence-of-blocked-lease was a real soak bug that this gap class produces.
`ContentAddressedMetadataStorage`'s `IMetadataStorage` overrides are exercised end-to-end only via `gtest_ca_wiring.cpp` and stateless/integration tests, not per-override unit tests.

A regression test mirroring `CasPartWriteTxn.PutBlobWrongSizeFailsClosed` should arm a backend that throws `SlowDown` on the `.meta` key and assert the freshness-meta write survives within the retry budget, pinning the S22 fix.

The 2026-07-17 codex-review triage's proposed fix-wave order prioritized finding №4 (condemn-marker load-bearing, the one reachable shared-pool data-loss class) first, then 19c (emu token etag-seeding), №5 (prune union), №22 (GC config bounds), №9 (decommission tail fencing), №7 (pool-UUID recheck), №16 (file_view fallback), №1 (unconditional-fallback guard), and paired №8/№10 (TSan-relevant lifecycle races) before the batch of small contract/hygiene fixes.

The condemned-evidence copy-forward design has a queued (not-yet-executed) validation task: a fresh soak run on a clean pool replaying the S13-adjacent kill-restart chaos, with the attach path expected to recover — verified by grepping for `BlobCopyForward` events and confirming zero "table will remain readonly" occurrences without recovery.

The source-layout refactoring design defers a backlog of deliberately-not-done improvements: a constructor config struct for the pool facade's ~25 positional parameters, flattening `SingleWriterSlot` into `MountLeaseKeeper` if no second subclass appears, and retiring vestiges like `ShardIncarnation` and the unreachable `CasNs::Server`.

Stage-B has two non-gating follow-ups scheduled after the T9 closeout: F1, a post-baseline mechanical split of `CasGc.cpp` and `CasRefLedger.cpp` along existing seams (request-count/order goldens captured before and rerun unchanged after); and F2, pre-upstream sanitation that strips branch-local documentation references and coordination markers from production code while keeping each rationale, starting from a measured 76-reference comment inventory and remeasuring before declaring it clean.; Stage-B follow-up Task F1 (outside the Stage-B verdict) is a purely mechanical split of `CasGc.cpp` and `CasRefLedger.cpp` (each ~4000 lines) along their existing semantic seams (GC: phases/fold/janitor; ledger: writer lanes/recovery/publication), gated by request-count/order equivalence goldens captured before any code moves and rerun unchanged afterward — no lifecycle or runtime boundary redesign.; Stage-B follow-up Task F2 (before upstreaming) is a sanitation sweep that strips branch-local references (task/review/finding numbers, BACKLOG, "superpowers") from production code and operator-visible strings, keeping the underlying reason but deleting the citation, verified by `git grep` measuring the baseline (~76 references) down to zero.
The S3-native staging plan's memory fast-path (spec §7) is explicitly deferred out of the plan as a separable optimization, noted for a follow-on.
